fill.obs_text: Qualifiers stand with this group in most of its verses and reach the words beside the member, not the member. The negators reach other words: in Gen 41:31 the negator of unknown reaches the plenty (the plenty will be unknown by reason of the famine), in Num 18:32 negation reaches bearing sin, profaning and dying, in Pro 3:30 the negator of the proverb reaches contending, and in Act 28:18 no reaches the ground for the death penalty, so that in this verse the negated word is the member's own object. Degree words reach the famine (very severe in Gen 41:31 and 47:13), frequency words reach the reasoning (three Sabbaths in Act 17:2, every Sabbath in Act 18:4, every day in Act 17:17, three months in Act 19:8), and in Mar 12:24 the not and neither-nor reach the knowledge that Jesus says is lacking. In Jam 3:17 the neighbours (from above, first, pure) qualify the wisdom, of which being open to reason is one trait. In 1Cor 13:11 child reaches the reckoning as a child's. In 1Pe 3:15 and 1Jo 3:8 no qualifier stands near the member.

fill.obs_text: The entities named in the verses of this group are divine and human. Divine: the Lord (Job 1:9, Isa 1:18, 1Pe 3:15), God (Job 1:9, Mar 12:24, Act 19:8, 2Ti 1:6, 1Pe 3:15, 1Jo 3:8), Jesus and Christ (Mar 12:24, Luk 9:47, Eph 3:1, 1Ti 1:16). Human: Joshua and the men (Jos 5:4), Solomon and David (1Ki 11:27), Job (Job 1:9), a man (Pro 3:30, 1Cor 13:11), Nebuchadnezzar (Dan 4:34), the men who came for Peter (Act 10:21), the disciples (Act 19:9, Luk 9:47), Paul's brothers (1Th 3:7). The reasoning in the verses of Acts is Paul's, addressed to hearers, and the grounds in the letters are Paul's, addressed to readers. This record does not compare the group with the others.

fill.obs_text: The direction of the reasoning and of the ground given is by the verses stated in four ways. The grounds of Paul's letters (Eph 3:1, 1Th 3:7, 1Ti 1:16, 2Ti 1:6) run from Paul to those he writes to, and in 1Ti 1:16 from Christ's mercy to him as an example. The reasoning of Acts (Act 19:8, 19:9) runs from Paul to the hearers in the synagogue, and the reasoning of Isa 1:18 from the Lord to the people. In Luk 9:47 and Mar 12:24 it runs from Jesus' knowing to the disciples' or the Sadducees' reasoning or error, and in Dan 4:34 it is the king's own reason returning to him. The cause given in Jos 5:4 and 1Ki 11:27 stands with a human act, and in Job 1:9 and Pro 3:30 the denial of a cause is said by Satan of Job and by the proverb of a man.

fill.obs_text: The surface reason carries many codes in this group and the verses show two senses. In one it names a ground or cause: H6440I in Gen 41:31 and 47:13, H5921A in Num 18:32 and 1Sa 20:29, H1697M in Jos 5:4 and 1Ki 11:27, H2600 for no reason in Job 1:9 and Pro 3:30, G1223 and G5124 in Mar 12:24, 1Th 3:5, 1Th 3:7 and 1Jo 3:8, G0156 in Act 10:21, 28:18, 28:20 and 2Ti 1:6, G1352 in Rom 15:22, G5484 in Eph 3:1 and 3:14, G0302 with G2596 in Act 18:14, G1519 in 1Jo 3:8 and G1961 in Eze 19:10. In the other it names the mind's working: H4486 the king's reason in Dan 4:34 and 4:36, H3198 the arguing of a case in Isa 1:18, G2138 the being open to reason in Jam 3:17, and G3056 the account of a hope in 1Pe 3:15. The surface is therefore double: a cause that stands outside the mind, and a working of the mind.
